articles.title: Início da temporada de cruzeiros é adiado por atraso de navio no Porto | G1
articles.standfirst: Temporada no Porto de Santos foi adiada de 23 para 30 de outubro. A mudança ocorreu devido ao atraso do navio Buenavista.
articles.summary: Inicialmente previsto para atracar no Porto de Santos no dia 23 de outubro, o Navio Buenavista chegará ao litoral paulista no dia 27 de outubro, segundo a Corazul.
articles.body:
Temporada de cruzeiros no Porto de Santos tem início programado para outubro — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Santos

A temporada de cruzeiros 2026/2027 no Porto de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, inicialmente prevista para começar no dia 23 de outubro, foi adiada para o dia 30 de outubro. A mudança aconteceu em razão do atraso da chegada do primeiro cruzeiro, o navio Buenavista, da empresa espanhola Corazul.

🚢 O Navio Buenavista tem capacidade para 2 mil passageiros e deve realizar 39 escalas no Porto de Santos durante a temporada 2026/2027, com embarques em Santos e no Rio de Janeiro.

A Corazul informou, em nota, que o Buenavista encontra-se atualmente próximo ao porto da Cidade do Cabo, África do Sul. Sujeito às condições meteorológicas, espera-se que o navio chegue a Santos em 27 de outubro.

Segundo a empresa, "alterações de horários não são incomuns na indústria de cruzeiros, particularmente durante o reposicionamento intercontinental, e neste caso foram devidas principalmente às condições marítimas e atrasos nas autorizações administrativas por parte de agências governamentais em outros países".

O Concais, responsável pela administração do Terminal Marítimo de Passageiros Giusfredo Santini, informou, em nota, que a primeira viagem do Navio Buenavista terá Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e Búzios (RJ) como escalas. O retorno da embarcação a Santos está previsto para o dia 2 de novembro.

A Corazul, responsável pela embarcação, informou que também está planejando um possível cruzeiro de apresentação, exclusivo para convidados, entre os dias 28 e 30 de outubro, período em que o navio estará atracado no cais santista. A confirmação da realização ainda depende da conclusão de procedimentos necessários para o início das operações da temporada.

De acordo com o Concais, após a atualização do calendário, a temporada passa a contar com 163 escalas em 102 dias de operação. No período entre 30 de outubro e 4 de abril, dez navios diferentes estão previstos para passar pelo Porto de Santos.

Entre os dez previstos, seis farão escalas, com embarque e desembarque em Santos, enquanto os outros quatro operarão em trânsito, com o desembarque dos passageiros para visitar a região, retornando às embarcações ao fim do tempo estipulado.

A expectativa da entidade é que a movimentação durante a temporada gire em torno de 900 mil passageiros , reunindo embarques, desembarques e passageiros em trânsito. Além disso, a movimentação econômica é estimada em R$ 1,5 bilhão e deve gerar 46 mil empregos, segundo o Concais.

articles.title: Por que Trump suspendeu várias sanções contra a Rússia | G1
articles.standfirst: O presidente dos EUA paralisou temporariamente muitas das restrições a Moscou, recentemente aprovadas pelo Congresso, sob a justificativa de preocupações com a "segurança nacional".
articles.summary: Trump suspende sanções contra a Rússia citando segurança nacional, enquanto Zelensky critica a medida e o polêmico acordo para importação de diesel russo.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , bloqueou diversas sanções contra a Rússia dois dias antes de as medidas entrarem em vigor, em meio ao agravamento de um impasse com o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky .

As sanções haviam sido aprovadas pelo Congresso dos EUA e transformadas em lei por Trump em setembro.

No entanto, na noite de sexta-feira (16), o presidente americano emitiu uma ordem executiva afirmando que a suspensão de algumas dessas medidas atendia ao "interesse nacional" dos EUA — uma decisão que provocou reações contrárias de legisladores americanos.

Zelensky lamentou que os EUA tenham decidido "ignorar completamente" as sanções.

As relações entre Washington e Kiev se deterioraram após os EUA firmarem um acordo controverso para a importação de diesel russo.

A Ucrânia acusou, então, a administração Trump de retirar um apoio militar fundamental ao país na guerra contra a Rússia.

Trump e Zelensky trocaram críticas ácidas um sobre o outro nos últimos dias.

O presidente da Ucrânia declarou que era bom estar entre "líderes de verdade" durante uma cúpula da União Europeia, depois que Trump afirmou que Zelensky era "mais difícil de lidar" do que o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin.

A nova lei de sanções dos EUA teve como alvo a economia russa, e conferiu a Trump amplos poderes para impor tarifas de até 100% sobre importações provenientes dos cinco maiores compradores de petróleo e gás da Rússia — com destaque para a China e a Índia.

A medida também incluiu sanções contra autoridades russas de alto escalão, incluindo Putin, e também contra instituições financeiras russas, além da chamada "frota fantasma" de Moscou — um conjunto de embarcações utilizadas para contornar embargos já existentes.

No entanto, muitas dessas disposições foram agora suspensas por Trump.

O representante russo Kirill Dmitriev classificou a suspensão como "um momento importante e verdadeiramente histórico".

Em uma publicação no X, ele afirmou que as sanções teriam causado "danos graves", principalmente aos EUA e ao mercado global, e que a cooperação econômica beneficia as duas nações.

Representantes do Partido Democrata, incluindo o congressista pela Virgínia, Don Beyer, criticaram a medida e acusaram Trump de capitular diante de Moscou e de virar as costas para Kiev e Zelensky.

"A mais recente rendição de Trump a Putin trai, mais uma vez, nossos parceiros ucranianos e desafia a clara intenção do Congresso, expressa em uma legislação concebida para punir a Rússia por sua guerra de agressão ilegal", escreveu Beyer no X.

É provável que a medida provoque ainda mais indignação na Ucrânia, onde Zelensky tem enfatizado, há muito tempo, a necessidade de sanções rigorosas para limitar os recursos que a Rússia pode utilizar em seu esforço de guerra.

Zelensky declarou, na manhã de sábado (17/10), que as sanções "poderiam ter ajudado enormemente" e que a lei "deveria ter exercido uma pressão verdadeiramente eficaz sobre a Rússia para pôr fim a esta guerra".

Ele mencionou os ataques russos ocorridos na noite de sexta-feira para sábado (17/10) contra 15 instalações energéticas ucranianas — que provocaram cortes de energia em várias regiões — e afirmou: "A Rússia está tentando causar um apagão na Ucrânia, justamente antes do inverno."

Zelensky ressaltou que é "importante que todos na América também vejam o que realmente está acontecendo".

Zelensky e Trump trocaram farpas recentemente — Foto: EPA

Mais tarde, o presidente ucraniano disse a repórteres que acreditava que a administração Trump suspenderia mais sanções contra a Rússia.

Ele também afirmou que negociadores ucranianos conversaram com seus homólogos americanos na sexta-feira (16/10) e que as equipes dos países poderiam se reunir na próxima semana.

Trump foi inicialmente criticado por Zelensky e pelos aliados europeus da Ucrânia por suspender temporariamente algumas sanções dos EUA para permitir a importação de diesel russo, em uma tentativa de reduzir os preços de energia nos Estados Unidos, que dispararam por causa da guerra contra o Irã.

O presidente americano passou meses lidando com as consequências políticas do conflito no Oriente Médio, que fez com que os custos dos combustíveis subissem drasticamente às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA.

A inflação crescente prejudicou a imagem de Trump diante do público americano.

Zelensky sugeriu que o acordo equivalia a um investimento dos EUA no esforço de guerra da Rússia.

A cidade de Zaporizhzhia esteve entre as regiões atingidas por ataques russos recentes — Foto: Reuters

Poucos dias depois, Trump afirmou que tanto a Rússia quanto a Ucrânia haviam concordado com um "cessar-fogo energético" para facilitar a exportação de diesel russo.

Ambas as nações têm atacado intensamente a infraestrutura energética uma da outra.

Kiev afirma que o objetivo é limitar as receitas da máquina de guerra russa, enquanto Moscou alega que atinge apenas instalações utilizadas pelos militares ucranianos.

Zelensky expressou, inicialmente, surpresa com o anúncio de Trump e disse que Kiev interromperia os ataques caso a Rússia fizesse o mesmo.

Após três dias marcados por novos ataques russos, Kiev retomou suas investidas contra refinarias de petróleo na Rússia.

Isso provocou uma condenação contundente por parte de Trump, que classificou os ataques como uma "vergonha".

Zelensky respondeu dizendo que estava "apenas defendendo os interesses da Ucrânia".

As preocupações de que Trump esteja alinhado à Rússia intensificaram-se após problemas no funcionamento de um sistema de satélites fornecido pelos EUA, que era utilizado pela Ucrânia.

Na semana passada, a Starlink restringiu, de forma repentina e inesperada, a velocidade com que drones podiam operar e mantinham a conexão com a internet.

Segundo a Ucrânia, isso prejudicou algumas missões no campo de batalha e dificultou a capacidade de Kiev de se defender contra ataques russos.

Durante o período de lentidão, a Rússia lançou diversos ataques letais contra a Ucrânia — tanto os moradores quanto o governo afirmaram que não houve qualquer aviso prévio.

Zelensky declarou na sexta-feira (16/0) que a velocidade da Starlink ainda não havia sido totalmente restabelecida.

Trump negou ter interrompido o compartilhamento de informações de inteligência ou ter reduzido, deliberadamente, a velocidade da rede Starlink na Ucrânia.

Autoridades ucranianas confirmaram que, nas últimas 24 horas, pelo menos nove pessoas morreram e cerca de 60 ficaram feridas em ataques russos em todo o país.

Elas informaram também que, na manhã de sábado (17/10), um motorista de ambulância foi morto e outras 20 pessoas ficaram feridas em ataques russos à cidade de Kherson.

O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia afirmou ter como alvo instalações ligadas ao setor de defesa ucraniano — o que inclui siderúrgicas, uma subestação elétrica e um navio de carga no Mar Negro.

articles.title: Trabalho escravo em Brasília: MPT processa diplomata e filho | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso será analisado pela Justiça do Trabalho. Funcionária de Vera Lúcia Barrouin e do filho dela, Rodrigo Barrouin, prestava serviços em tempo integral, sem folgas regulares ou registro em carteira.
articles.summary: Caso será analisado pela Justiça do Trabalho. Funcionária de Vera Lúcia e Rodrigo Barrouin prestava serviços em tempo integral, sem folgas regulares ou registro em carteira.
articles.body:
Fachada do Ministério Público do Trabalho no DF (MPT-DF) — Foto: Messias Carvalho/MPT-10

O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) apresentou uma ação civil pública contra a diplomata aposentada Vera Lúcia Barrouin e o filho dela, Rodrigo Barrouin , por exploração de trabalho análogo à escravidão em uma casa no Lago Sul , em Brasília , área nobre da capital.

Segundo o MPT, uma funcionária, de 68 anos, prestava serviços domésticos e de assistência à Vera, que possui Alzheimer, em tempo integral, sem folgas regulares ou registro em carteira .

A ação será analisada pela Justiça do Trabalho. O g1 tenta contato com a defesa de Vera Lúcia e Rodrigo Barrouin.

Segundo apurado pelo MPT, a funcionária trabalha para a família há 35 anos e relatou que desejava sair daquele trabalho, por ser muito pesado.

Além disso, a funcionária relatou que permanece na casa da ex-diplomata em tempo integral para cuidar dela e limpar a residência, inclusive nos finais de semana e em feriados. A mulher vai para sua própria casa apenas nas férias.

A funcionária também relatou que escondia o celular, para Vera Lúcia não tomar o aparelho.

O MPT pede a condenação ao pagamento de indenizações, que somam R$ 800 mil , por:

dano moral individual: valor não inferior a R$ 500 mil pago diretamente à vítima;

dano moral coletivo: valor não inferior a R$ 300 mil pela lesão difusa à sociedade, a ser destinado a entidades sociais.

articles.title: 72-year old Vaidehi Chandrasekar won gold at the 2026 World Nature Photography Award for clicking a giraffe expelling a perfect arc of water after drinking in Botswana
articles.summary: A giraffe takes a drink, raises its head and sends water droplets flying through the air. For most observers, it might be a fleeting wildlife moment.
articles.body: A giraffe takes a drink, raises its head and sends water droplets flying through the air. For most observers, it might be a fleeting wildlife moment. For 72-year-old Vaidehi Chandrasekar, it became an award-winning photograph. Titled 'Water Ballet', the image captured the water forming a near-perfect circle in the golden light of sunset in Botswana. Chandrasekar won gold in the Behaviour – Mammals category at the 2026 World Nature Photography Awards, with the organisers and The Straits Times confirming the photograph’s distinction.The image was taken in the Makgadikgadi Pans National Park, where the dry landscape and fading sunlight provided the backdrop for the unusual scene. According to the awards website, the giraffe bent its long legs to lower its neck towards the water. After drinking, it lifted its head and swished, sending a stream of water into an arc that appeared almost circular before the droplets fell back to the ground.The sunlight illuminated the airborne water and outlined the giraffe against the darker background. The result was a photograph that combined animal behaviour, timing and light in a single frame.A rare moment at the water’s edgeChandrasekar told The Straits Times that she had photographed giraffes before, but seeing one expel so much water was unusual. She described herself as lucky to have captured the moment. Her entry to the competition explained that she wanted to record the interplay between the golden light and the movement of the water.The photograph’s title, 'Water Ballet', reflects the arc created by the droplets as they moved through the air. The scene was brief, requiring the photographer to be ready as the giraffe finished drinking and raised its head.According to photography publication 'Digital Camera World', Chandrasekar used a Nikon Z9 mirrorless camera with a 400mm lens. The image was captured at a shutter speed of 1/1000 second, with an aperture of f/5.6 and ISO 400. The fast shutter speed helped freeze the movement of the water droplets, preserving the shape of the arc.The technical details provide context for how the fleeting scene was recorded, but the photograph’s impact also depended on the natural conditions. The low sun illuminated the droplets from behind, creating the bright outline and golden reflections that distinguish the image.From retirement to wildlife photographyChandrasekar, a Singapore permanent resident, became more involved in photography in 2019 after retiring from a job in systems design support, The Straits Times reported. She and her husband, who is also in his seventies, learnt photographic techniques through YouTube videos and trial and error.Wildlife photography has since taken the couple to destinations where they can observe animals in their natural habitats. Chandrasekar has travelled to photograph animals such as leopards and polar bears, while also photographing birds that visit Singapore during migration seasons.She told the newspaper that she often follows information shared by other photographers about where particular birds can be found. Fellow photographers have also helped her learn how to capture images of birds, whose constant movement makes getting the right angle challenging.The Botswana safari, however, was not without its difficulties. Chandrasekar described camping on the trip with her husband as challenging, but said they continued despite the demands of the experience. Her plans for future wildlife photography include seeing orangutans in Indonesia and penguins in Antarctica. She said that the couple had a long list of places and animals they hoped to experience while they could still travel.A gold-winning photographThe World Nature Photography Awards announced its 2026 winners in February, with thousands of entries submitted by photographers from 51 countries across six continents. Chandrasekar received the gold award in Behaviour – Mammals for 'Water Ballet', while the competition’s overall World Nature Photographer of the Year title went to Australian photographer Jono Allen for Mãhina, an image of a rare white humpback whale calf swimming with its mother in the waters around Tonga. Chandrasekar’s award was therefore a category win, rather than the competition’s grand prize.The awards cover a range of subjects, from animal portraits and wildlife behaviour to landscapes, underwater photography and the relationship between people and nature. The winning images are intended to showcase the diversity of the natural world and encourage greater awareness of wildlife and conservation.For Chandrasekar, that conservation aspect was one reason the competition appealed to her. The photographer said that she believed photographs could help people learn about animals and understand why they should be left undisturbed in their habitats. The awards programme partners with environmental organisation Ecologi to plant a tree for every entry, according to the newspaper’s report.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘Taking away right to vote, protest’: Uddhav backs opposition's ‘regime change’ call against government
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Saturday backed the opposition’s call for 'regime change', saying a government that takes away
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Saturday backed the opposition’s call for 'regime change', saying a government that takes away people’s right to express themselves through voting and protests needs to be changed.“Police are assaulting youth and women, tearing their clothes. Such a regime needs to be buried,” he said, referring to alleged police action against protesters in the national capital.Addressing the Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Patrakar Parishad, Thackeray questioned the deployment of a large number of police personnel in Delhi during protests called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other parties.“Have thousands of police personnel been deployed in Delhi to ‘play dandia’?” he asked.Taking a swipe at the BJP over media reports of a cockroach effigy being burnt during Dussehra celebrations, Thackeray said that those who claim to have brought Ram are scared of cockroaches.“We are here to change the regime,” he asserted.Thackeray’s remarks came amid a political row over the opposition’s protests against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The call intensified after senior advocate Prashant Bhushan called for “regime change”, arguing that spreading “disaffection” against a government was not a crime in a democracy.“This government keeps on saying this is the opposition's operation of regime change. We are only appealing to save the electoral democracy in this country. If such barbarism continues, there will definitely be a regime change. We all want a regime change. Is there anything wrong with that? Regime change is a democratic right of every citizen, and creating disaffection against the government is not an offence,” Bhushan had said at a press conference on Thursday.Dipke was granted conditional bail on Saturday and asked to sign a peace bond. He had been detained on Friday after stepping out of his home in Delhi’s Jhandewalan area to join the CJP’s “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest at Connaught Place. articles.title: ‘No reasons are forthcoming’: HC on Centre’s denial to Mann’s France visit
articles.summary: Punjab and Haryana HC lets Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann visit France for SIAL Paris, faulting MEA for denying clearance citing a vague “political angle.”
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: The Punjab and Haryana high court has observed that the MEA had “not explained” the political angle it cited while turning down political clearance to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann for his visit to France.The court released the detailed order on Saturday, a day after it allowed Punjab govt’s plea to let Mann fly to France for SIAL Paris 2026, a food and beverage innovation trade fair to be attended by the state-run Markfed.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) had refused to let Mann visit France, citing a “political angle”. In its detailed order, the court said: “It has not been explained what that political angle/viewpoint is, and whether political clearance means examining the application from a political angle. No reasons are forthcoming.”Justice Tribhuvan Dahiya rejected Centre’s justification that there was no proper invitation from the French govt and the CM had no functional role to perform during the proposed visit. The bench held that the reasons subsequently offered in an affidavit could not be used to justify the original decision.The HC allowed the petition filed by the Punjab govt challenging the denial of political clearance to a three-member delegation comprising the CM, the chief secretary and the principal secretary to the CM for a visit to Paris from Oct 17 to 21 to promote trade and attend the SIAL food exhibition.The court observed that the contention regarding the absence of a proper invitation from the foreign govt “cannot be accepted” in view of a Sept 22 letter sent by SIAL to the French Embassy in India. The letter stated, “We are very pleased to count among our visitors Mr. Bhagwant Mann ... (w)e are convinced that this is an opportunity for Mr. Bhagwant Mann to establish professional contacts with French and international visitors and to negotiate contracts.”Rejecting the second justification that the CM had no functional role during the visit, the bench observed that it cannot be accepted as “he himself is heading the delegation”.The bench questioned the requirement for the ministry to examine the CM’s functional role during the visit. “Further, it has not been explained as to why is there a requirement for the ministry to examine functional role of the chief minister during the proposed visit,” it observed. “The requirement appears to be superfluous for the reason the clearance has been denied due to ‘political angle’ alone, and not on any functional aspect of the dignitary’s visit,” the bench added.The high court also relied on the Supreme Court Constitution Bench judgment in Mohinder Singh Gill and another versus The Chief Election Commissioner, New Delhi and others, 1978 AIR Supreme Court 851, to emphasise that the “validity of an order must be judged by the reasons mentioned therein which cannot be supplemented by fresh reasons in the shape of an affidavit or otherwise”. “Accordingly, the reasons given in the affidavit filed on behalf the respondents cannot justify the order as the same do not find mention in the order,” it said.Opposing the petition, the Centre had submitted that granting or denying political clearance for foreign visits was MEA’s responsibility and depended on factors including bilateral relations, the prevailing political situation, the diplomatic climate and anti-India activities in or emanating from the country concerned.The Centre argued that reasons for refusing clearance were not always disclosed on the portal because of the sensitivity of matters affecting bilateral relations. It cited security concerns relating to the CM and contended that in the absence of a proper bilateral invitation from the foreign govt, the required security arrangements and protocol would not be available.Punjab govt had argued that the refusal was arbitrary, as no opportunity had been given to explain the position and no reasons had been assigned. It also contended that the decision had been communicated at the eleventh hour, frustrating the proposed visit.The court noted that the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) had confirmed Markfed’s participation in the SIAL food exhibition and allotted it a stall.The HC noted that Markfed was to pay for the visit. The stated purpose of the visit included facilitating direct engagement with international buyers, importers, food companies and investors, promoting investment opportunities and encouraging the adoption of international best practices in food processing.Punjab govt had applied for political clearance through the MEA’s e-Pol Clearance System on Sept 9, enclosing relevant documents and explaining the purpose of the visit. articles.title: Govt orders monthly road safety reviews, CAG audit of safety funds
articles.summary: Telangana govt mandates monthly district road safety reviews, online fund tracking and CAG audits of road safety funds to curb accidents and fatalities.
articles.body: Hyderabad: The Telangana govt has issued comprehensive guidelines for the administration and monitoring of state and district road safety funds, making monthly meetings of district road safety committees mandatory and requiring all fund accounts to be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). The guidelines were issued through a GO in accordance with the directives of Union ministry of road transport and highways. Transport minister Ponnam Prabhakar said the measures were aimed at strengthening road safety, preventing accidents and reducing fatalities across the state.Under the new framework, the road safety cess collected under the Telangana Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2026, will be credited to the Telangana road safety non-lapsable fund. The statutory state road safety council, headed by the chief minister with the transport minister as vice-chairman, will oversee the fund’s administration and management.Govt has also decided to extend the online accounting system to all districts to improve transparency in the utilisation of road safety funds. The system will enable authorities to monitor receipts and expenditure in real time. Accounts maintained at both state and district levels will be subject to mandatory CAG audits. Details of the funds and their utilisation will also be uploaded to Union road transport ministry’s portal, making them accessible to the Supreme Court committee on road safety.Road safety plan“As part of the new framework, district collectors have been directed to immediately activate district road safety committees and ensure that they meet every month. Each district will have to appoint a road safety coordinator and submit a district road safety plan outlining the measures proposed to improve safety,” Ponnam said.The police, health, roads and buildings, and education departments, along with GHMC, have been asked to appoint nodal officers to coordinate road safety measures within their respective jurisdictions. Several departments and agencies will also be required to submit quarterly action-taken reports to the lead agency for road safety.The police, health, roads and buildings, and education departments, along with the GHMC, have been asked to appoint nodal officers to coordinate road safety measures within their respective jurisdictions. articles.title: 'Do something. You can’t die like this': flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchar recounts cockpit attack
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Two hours into the flight from Dubai to Tel Avivi, flydubai commander, Capt Smit Machchar was checking landing time and fuel figures on the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Two hours into the flight from Dubai to Tel Avivi, flydubai commander, Capt Smit Machchar was checking landing time and fuel figures on the computer when something struck hard at the back of his head. He thought part of his Boeing 737’s cockpit roof had broken loose. Seconds later, as more blows rained in, he turned and saw it was his co-pilot. Bleeding, his vision shrunk to a few inches, he drifted in and out of consciousness during those fateful minutes when the aircraft went into a rapid descent, while the attack continued. “There was a moment I told myself, Smit, do something, you can’t die like this,” said the flydubai pilot, recounting the Sept 30 terror attack on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, which was diverted and landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The pilot said his memory of what followed is fragmented, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists. In his first extended account since the incident, given to Sky News Arabia on Sat evening, Machchar said an ordinary flight, with a co-pilot he was flying with for the first time, turned violent minutes after the man stood up to pray.It was a route he had flown many times. An augmented crew was on board, and the relief captain was to take over operating duties after landing. “Normal flight,” he told the channel. “It went on like a normal day till it wasn’t.”About two hours in, the relief captain had dropped by the cockpit to chat about rosters and flying hours when the co-pilot, who had stepped out for a toilet break, returned. A few minutes into their conversation, he said he wished to pray and asked the relief captain to step out. Machchar said such requests are accepted in the region when the flight is stable.The co-pilot asked the other Captain to step out, stood up behind him and began praying. “Out of respect, I did not look back. I was checking the landing time and fuel figures on the computer, the routine background tasks of the monitoring pilot. Suddenly there was a very hard hit at the back of my head,” he said. “It was something very strong and hard. I didn’t know at that point what had hit me.” He fell forward, and his mind reached for training. “My first thought was, okay, something has broken from the aircraft roof, and it has been a catastrophic damage. I was planning to regain my composure and check my systems.”The blows kept coming. Within seconds his vision had narrowed to a few inches, he said. When he glanced back, he understood. “He was saying something while hitting me, but I could not understand.” Machchar unbuckled and tried to shield himself, taking a blow on his hand. “That’s when something flipped,” he said. He screamed for the relief captain and, since the door switch was within reach, managed to open it. He lost consciousness for the first time soon after. He recalled hearing shouting between the co-pilot and the other crew before the door shut again, with the co-pilot threatening to hit them too.It was after this, he said, that he heard the engines spool down and felt the aircraft pitch into a dive. “I don’t have to see the instruments, I can have my eyes closed and still know the engines are spooling down and the aircraft is going down. Every pilot will tell you this.”Drifting in and out of consciousness from blood loss, he said, he reached a point of decision. “I told myself, Smit, do something. You can’t die like this. I’m not saying I accepted my death. It was like, do something, otherwise...” The pilot added his memory of what followed is fragmentary, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists. He said he remembers locking his legs against something and pushing toward the door. He said he remembers then lying face down between the cockpit and the galley, the door open, passengers panicking.Machchar credited his colleague for taking the controls and recovering the aircraft, calling it something he will carry “till I die.” Asked about the speculation over how the plane was saved, he declined to single anyone out. “Everyone did the best in their capacity,” he said, including crew and passengers.He said he knew he was out of danger only when the aircraft touched down. Until then a doctor on board and his crew kept him conscious. “At that point, what I was more focused on was to not give up on life. You say you see flashes and stuff like that (speaking about death). You just remember the person who matters the most,” he said. The first call he made was to his 2-year old son. In the days that followed the incident, he continued to get flashes of the first blow. The commander added that he has been getting better with each passing day and can now sit and have conversations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: France protests: Violent clashes, looting and buildings ablaze as over 1,000 arrested
articles.summary: Disorder broke out in cities across the country on a day in which more than half a million joined cost of living protests.
articles.body:
Violence broke out across France on Saturday during the latest day of demonstrations against education standards and the cost of living.

At least 1,200 people were arrested during what the French government described as an "escalation in violence" alongside an estimated 550,000 taking to the streets.

In Paris, there were significant clashes into the evening with riot police, who used tear gas and water cannon on crowds.

Buildings were set alight in the capital and other areas, including in Limoges where a large fire in the town hall caused the roof to partly collapse.

Looting broke out in several cities, with widespread vandalism targeted against city halls and businesses also reported.

Sixty law enforcement officers were injured, including two who were taken to hospital unconscious, France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said.

In Paris, the main march appeared to be largely peaceful during the afternoon. A group of young people told the BBC they were "pacifists" who are "just trying to make things change, but nothing is moving".

However, as the day wore on some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles, including in iconic locations in the city centre like the Place de la République.

Shops were ransacked, at least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups.

Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons.

In Lyon, Mayor Grégory Doucet said the burning of the city's tourist office was "a tragedy" for the city, telling BFMTV "it breaks our hearts because it's a very iconic, well-known historic building".

Local police said "hostile individuals" prevented firefighters from safely tackling the blaze.

Fire crews also battled the fire at Limoges town hall, which the local prefecture said caused part of the building to collapse.

A young man "had his hand blown off by a grenade" in Saint-Étienne, the south-eastern city's Mayor Régis Juanico said on social media, adding: "Such a tragedy should never have happened."

The interior ministry said the protests involved "targeted acts of violence" from "hooded individuals" in places, including parts of the capital and also Marseille, Rennes, Toulouse and Angers.

Damage to buildings was reported across France, including in Grenoble, Avignon, Pau, Montpellier and Valence.

Clothes and food shops were raided in Paris, while an Apple store in Lille was broken into and emptied.

Footage authenticated by BBC Verify showed a tourist train in Grenoble being driven by masked men along a narrow street in the city centre towards at least three riot police officers.

Hundreds of thousands of students have protested in recent weeks over staff shortages and dilapidated facilities in the country's lycées - secondary schools attended by 15 to 18-year-olds.

On Saturday, their numbers were bolstered by trade union members and other protest groups.

These groups include the so-called gilets jaunes 'yellow vest' movement, who demonstrated against cost-of-living hikes for over a year from 2018 - becoming one of the longest-lived protest movements in French history.

While France is no stranger to outbreaks of protest and disorder, this round comes as the country heads into a period of deep political uncertainty.

French President Emmanuel Macron will leave office next year and polls suggest April's presidential election could come down to a fight between the leader of the National Rally, Marine Le Pen, and Jean-Luc Mélenchon of the hard-left La France Insoumise party.

The latter took part in demonstrations in France and later accused police officers of "unleashing" on protesters, while condemning looting and arson.

France's Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said his comments were "dangerous and cynical".

He earlier said police had faced "violence of extreme intensity" and some groups were using the protests as a "warm-up" for the presidential elections, adding: "No-one will impose their political agenda through violence."

Le Pen said "legitimate demands" voiced by protesters had been "held hostage by the far left", accusing Mélenchon of fuelling the violence.

French President Emmanuel Macron said: "Those who have broken, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished."

The government has made apparent attempts at concessions, with Education Minister Édouard Geffray promising 3,000 extra supply teachers, during a television interview on 8 October.

However, the protests have continued and intensified.

articles.title: Zelensky says Ukraine is ‘ready to negotiate’
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday expressed his openness to engaging in U.S.-led negotiations to end the yearslong Russia-Ukraine war after President Trump placed a hold on Russian sanctions days before they were set to go into effect. “The American negotiating track will continue,” Zelensky wrote on the social platform X. “We’re counting on them…
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday expressed his openness to engaging in U.S.-led negotiations to end the yearslong Russia-Ukraine war after President Trump placed a hold on Russian sanctions days before they were set to go into effect.

“The American negotiating track will continue,” Zelensky wrote on the social platform X . “We’re counting on them to put more pressure on [Russian President Vladimir] Putin, not on us. Otherwise, it’s simply unfair.”

The Ukrainian leader said his country is “ready to negotiate anywhere” and in “any format” with the U.S.

“What matters is peace,” he wrote. “The American side has given us a signal that our meeting with them can happen next week.”

Last month, top U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff traveled to Russia and Ukraine to meet with each country’s leader in hopes of jumpstarting talks to end this yearslong war.

However, the two sides have continued to strike each other’s energy infrastructure , placing an even greater strain on global energy supplies already tightened amid the Iran war.

Additionally, the Ukrainian leader said that the U.S. was “working” on setting up a trilateral meeting with Putin, adding that one possibility for this discussion could be at the G20 summit in Miami in December.

“But there has been no confirmation yet from Russia or from the United States,” he added. “The meeting could also take place in one of the European countries. I know that the Europeans are starting contacts about this. We’ll see how things turn out a little later.”

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

On Friday evening, Trump signed an executive order waiving sanctions on Russia set to be imposed under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 . The sweeping legislative package sought to place financial pressure on Russia to wind down its military operations against Ukraine.

The order stated that this hold measure was “in the national interests of the United States,” without specifying a reason.

This move followed Trump’s decision last week to ease sanctions on Russian diesel amid rising fuel costs in the U.S. and abroad. The Trump administration is under pressure to address Americans’ affordability concerns less than three weeks out from the midterm elections.

Zelensky warned earlier Saturday morning that these relief actions could aid what he described as a Russian effort to “cause a blackout in Ukraine.”

“Pressure is needed to stop this. A U.S. sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin – all of this only encourages him to keep attacking,” he wrote on X . “We must not give up ground.”

articles.title: At least 17 dead in crush at Hindu festival event in India
articles.summary: Many more have been injured at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark a Hindu festival.
articles.body:
At least 17 people have been killed and many more injured in a crush at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark the Hindu festival of Durga Puja, officials say.

The incident occurred during sudden rainfall, which witnesses say prompted a surge of people to try to seek shelter.

West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari said a seven-year-old girl was among the dead, and that 25 people were being treated for injuries.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described it as a "tragic" incident and said the regional government was providing help to affected families.

Six of the dead have been identified, Adhikari said.

A senior police official told the AFP news agency that an announcement caused "commotion" after it started raining and the crowd started "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.".

Deadly crowd incidents, including during religious festivals, are not uncommon in India due to poor management and lack of adequate safety precautions.

Two years ago, 121 people were killed in Uttar Pradesh during a Hindu religious gathering.

articles.title: A 1923 Methodist church in Australia later served as a Sunday school and dance school before becoming a three-bedroom home with a cathedral ceiling and coloured glass; it is now listed for $865,000 to $950,000
articles.summary: First, it was a church. Then it became something else, and then something else again.
articles.body: First, it was a church. Then it became something else, and then something else again. Now, the building at 72 The Crescent in Tyabb, Victoria, has found a new purpose as a three-bedroom home. Built in 1923, this former Methodist church has lived several lives. Now, the property, with historic character and modern comfort, is on the market. The guide price sits between $865,000 and $950,000, according to the listing.Inside the 1923 renovated home The building at 72 The Crescent started as a Methodist church in 1923, according to the listing. Over time, a Sunday school wing was added to it. At another point, it housed a dance school. Each stage added something, and the current owners have kept those layers visible rather than covering them up. That is a lot of uses for one building. The building is now a three-bedroom home. The owners have preserved its history while adding contemporary comfort.The heart of the home is the former church hall. This house has unique features that most homes cannot compete with: soaring cathedral ceilings, exposed structural timbers, original windows, coloured glass and polished floorboards. The living and dining areas sit beneath the roof, and the room is large enough for relaxed weeknights as well as large-scale entertaining.The contemporary kitchen sits at one end. It is quite spacious and has plenty of cabinets, a substantial island, a dishwasher and a freestanding cooker. The listing says the finishes are modern, and they contrast with the warmth of the older walls around them. Few kitchens get to sit inside a space that looks like this.The bedrooms look different from the hall and other parts of the house. This wing was rebuilt into a practical, modern layout. The builders still kept some doors, skirtings and architectural details, so the rooms retain a visual link to the church. The massive main bedroom has a walk-in wardrobe, a private en suite and access to a secluded patio. The other two bedrooms also have walk-in wardrobes. They share a family bathroom, and there is a separate powder room nearby.One of the smaller original rooms now serves as the laundry. It was once used as the priest’s office, “where marriage documents were signed, a charming reminder of the building's past now thoughtfully incorporated into everyday life”, the listing says. The house also has separate heating and cooling systems.The outdoors are as mesmerising as the indoors. French doors open from the living space onto a broad entertaining deck. Beyond it sits a secure lawn and an established garden. “Views of surrounding trees and greenery create a wonderfully peaceful atmosphere”, the listing says.The property also includes a driveway, a double carport and an extra hardstand for larger vehicles. A separate outbuilding and former side rooms can hold bikes, garden tools and everyday items. “The flexible internal design also provides scope for future owners to adapt selected spaces to suit their needs, subject to any required approvals.”The guide price is between $865,000 and $950,000. The next owner not only inherits the home but also its rich history and the details that are still intact. articles.title: Seven years after the Manchester Arena attack, Ariana Grande sent Christmas gifts to children across four hospitals in the city, continuing a connection that reached beyond her concert stage
articles.summary: Ariana Grande’s relationship with Manchester did not end when the lights went down at the Manchester Arena in May 2017.
articles.body: Ariana Grande’s relationship with Manchester did not end when the lights went down at the Manchester Arena in May 2017. Seven years after the attack that killed 22 people following her concert, the singer continued a quiet tradition of sending Christmas gifts to children spending the holiday season in hospitals across Greater Manchester. In December 2024, the Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust charity confirmed that her donations had reached young patients at four hospitals.The gifts were distributed to babies, children and teenagers at Royal Manchester Children’s Hospital, Trafford General Hospital, Wythenshawe Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital. According to ITV News, the charity publicly thanked Grande and said it was grateful she had thought of its young patients at Christmas. The gesture was not a one-time act of generosity, but part of a connection that has continued since the tragedy.A bond formed in griefGrande was performing at the Manchester Arena on May 22, 2017, when a suicide bomber attacked the venue as concertgoers were leaving. Twenty-two people were killed and many more were injured, turning a night of music into one of the deadliest attacks in recent British history.In the days that followed, Grande returned to Manchester to organise the One Love Manchester benefit concert. The event raised money for the victims and their families, while also offering the city a moment of collective healing. Her response earned her honorary citizenship of Manchester in 2017, as per reports.The singer later spoke openly about the emotional toll of the attack. BBC News reported that Grande experienced post-traumatic stress disorder after the bombing, a reality that makes her continued support for Manchester’s hospitals especially meaningful.Christmas gifts for young patientsThe 2024 donation was confirmed by the Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust charity shortly before Christmas. It said the presents were being shared among babies, children and teenagers across the four hospitals, bringing a moment of comfort to families spending the festive period away from home.Royal Manchester Children’s Hospital has been a particular focus of Grande’s support. ITV News noted that she has maintained a long-standing relationship with the hospital since the 2017 attack, and that her gifts have reached patients across the wider Greater Manchester hospital network as well.For children in hospital, Christmas can be especially difficult. Medical routines, treatment schedules and separation from normal holiday celebrations can make the season feel distant. A gift from a globally known artist does not change those circumstances, but it can remind young patients and their families that they have not been forgotten.A tradition that has continuedThis was not the first time Grande had sent presents to Manchester’s hospitals. articles.title: Half a million protesters sweep France in major show of youth unrest
articles.summary: Clouds of tear gas fired by police filled the streets of Paris on Saturday, as anti-government protests stretched beyond the French capital.
articles.body: Clouds of tear gas fired by police filled the streets of Paris on Saturday, as anti-government protests stretched beyond the French capital. Some 550,000 protesters hit the streets across France, including 110,000 in Paris, interior minister Laurent Nunez said. Organizers estimated even higher turnout. Protests also took place in Rennes, Lyon and Marseilles this weekend. Photos emerged of people climbing atop historical statues and buildings set alight, with protesters in Lille and Marseilles reportedly breaking into government buildings as dusk fell. “There’s an accumulation of wealth and power that’s completely out of control,” one protester, who gave her name as Pauline, told CNN in Paris on Saturday. “We’re also here to support the youth. There are victories, but if we look at the bigger picture, it’s not going in the right direction,” the 36-year-old added. Another demonstrator complained of “less democracy” and a “concentration of power” under President Emmanuel Macron’s leadership. “There are billionaires who control the media,” Louise, 38, told CNN. “We are fighting to change things.” This weekend’s massive protests follow sweeping student-led rallies that gripped parts of France last month, sparking a broader, multi-coalition movement against crumbling schools, the spiking cost of living, and perceived government inaction. The rallies have become emblematic of long-simmering, intergenerational anger among people who say their calls for social and political change are going unmet by negligent governments. As night fell in Paris, groups of young people looted and started fires as the protest ended, prompting police to respond with tear gas and baton charges in the narrow streets. Macron condemned “sowers of chaos” for interfering with peaceful protest, and warned late on Saturday that “those who have broken, attacked (police) prefectures, as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished.” “We do not back down in the face of rioters and those who’ve come to attack law enforcement,” said the Paris Police Prefecture – the body that oversees the Paris Police Force, emergency services and various other administrative departments supervising unit – adding that its staffers stood “their ground with courage and professionalism.” At least 195 people have been detained so far, against the backdrop of mounting criticism over authorities’ forceful clamp down on demonstrators. Earlier in the week, police response to protests had left a 14-year-old boy with a fractured jaw. Another police officer was captured on camera using a headlock on a girl in the northwestern area of Alençon, an action now prohibited by law. A protester in the city of Saint-Étienne, about 40 miles southwest of Lyon, lost his hand during a march there on Saturday, a police source told CNN affiliate BFMTV. This is the second reported instance of a demonstrator losing their hand in the current wave of student protests. A student in the northeastern city of Lens lost his hand after reportedly picking up a grenade earlier this month, prompting the temporary suspension of one type of stun grenade by police. That ban, which still allowed police to use several different grenades, has now been rescinded. Overall, authorities said that the “vast majority of individuals” had demonstrated peacefully on Saturday, according to BFMTV. Posting on X, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the far-left La France Insoumise Party, emphasized that the majority of demonstrators on Sunday had made their point peacefully. “While news channels are flooded with images of violence in dozens of cities, everything is unfolding peacefully with tens of thousands of people calmly mobilized. Two worlds, two realities.” Youth activists led solidarity protests in Belgium, Albania and Italy on Saturday as well. Earlier this fall, high school students in France organized scattered protests demanding reduced class sizes, increased spending on teachers, investments in infrastructure designed to withstand the climate crisis and end to police violence against young people. In the past decade and a half, a rise in fertility coupled with funding cuts has led to more students, but fewer teachers in classrooms. The French Education Minister Edouard Geffray has met with student protesters multiple times in recent weeks, although an agreement is yet to be made.

articles.title: An Oregon couple had 14 acres too wet for hay but too dry for wildlife; they restored it into a wetland that attracted birds within days and helped reduce flooding on their ranch
articles.summary: For Heidi and Stan Gorden, ranchers at Bar GX Ranch in Bonanza, Oregon, a low-lying patch of land presented an unusual problem.
articles.body: For Heidi and Stan Gorden, ranchers at Bar GX Ranch in Bonanza, Oregon, a low-lying patch of land presented an unusual problem. It was too wet to cut hay but too dry to attract the wetland wildlife they wanted to see. Rather than continue struggling to use the area for agriculture, the couple explored whether restoring its natural wetland characteristics could make it more useful for wildlife and water management. In early 2024, they approached the US Fish and Wildlife Service and the Klamath Watershed Partnership for help. With conservation specialists helping secure funding, the 14-acre area was restored by autumn that year. Wildlife began using the habitat within days, and the wetland also helped reduce flooding elsewhere on the ranch, according to the federal agency.How an Oregon couple found a new purpose for difficult ranchlandThe Gordens' project began with a patch of low-lying land that presented challenges for their working ranch. It was too wet to cut hay, limiting its agricultural use, but it did not provide the conditions needed to attract the wetland wildlife they wanted to support. Wetlands can provide feeding and resting areas for birds and other wildlife, but their ecological value depends on factors such as water levels, vegetation and the availability of suitable habitat. The Gordens saw an opportunity to restore the area rather than continue trying to use it for hay production.In early 2024, they contacted the US Fish and Wildlife Service's Partners for Fish and Wildlife programme and the Klamath Watershed Partnership, a local conservation organisation. The partners worked with the couple to develop the restoration project and secure funding. Brian Hidden, from the federal agency's conservation programme, and Mark Johnson of the Klamath Watershed Partnership helped coordinate the effort. The restoration was completed by autumn 2024.How 14 acres were restored into a wetlandThe project focused on restoring approximately 14 acres at Bar GX Ranch. The aim was to turn a difficult-to-farm area into functioning wetland habitat that could support wildlife while helping manage water on the property. Instead of trying to make the entire patch suitable for cutting hay, the restoration gave the land a different role within the ranch. The area could provide habitat for birds and other animals while retaining its importance as part of the property's water system.The US Fish and Wildlife Service reported that the restoration was completed in autumn 2024. However, its published account does not provide a detailed description of the earthworks, water-control structures, planting methods or other technical measures used to restore the site. It also does not disclose the project's total cost or the amount of funding secured. The restoration was carried out with support from the Gordens' conservation partners, which helped make the project possible on privately owned working land.Ducks and shorebirds began using the restored habitat within daysWildlife began using the restored wetland within days of the project's completion, according to the US Fish and Wildlife Service. Ducks, shorebirds and pronghorn were among the animals observed in the area. Photographs accompanying the agency's report document several examples of wildlife at the site. These include Canada geese, a ruddy duck and white-faced ibis. Another photograph shows a sandhill crane flying over Canada geese feeding in the wetland.The arrival of wildlife so soon after the restoration provided an early indication that animals were using the habitat. Wetlands can offer birds access to food, shallow water and places to rest, depending on the conditions available at a particular site.The restored wetland also helped reduce floodingThe project had benefits beyond wildlife habitat. The US Fish and Wildlife Service reported that the restored wetland helped reduce flooding elsewhere on the ranch. Wetlands can hold excess water and slow its movement across a landscape. By providing space for water to collect, they can sometimes reduce the amount or speed of runoff reaching surrounding areas. The effects depend on factors such as the wetland's location, soil conditions, water levels and connections to nearby waterways.At Bar GX Ranch, the agency specifically reported reduced flooding in other parts of the property following the restoration. Its account does not quantify the reduction or state how much additional land became available for agricultural use. For the Gordens, the project addressed two concerns associated with the same patch of land: its limited usefulness for hay production and the need to support wetland wildlife. The restored area now serves as habitat while also contributing to water management on the ranch.How conservation partners helped make the project possibleThe restoration brought together the Gordens, the US Fish and Wildlife Service and the Klamath Watershed Partnership. Hidden represented the federal agency's Partners for Fish and Wildlife programme, while Johnson worked with the local conservation partnership. The federal programme works with private landowners to restore and improve wildlife habitat on their properties. Such assistance can help landowners access technical expertise and funding for conservation projects that might otherwise be difficult to undertake.In its report published on March 12, 2026, the US Fish and Wildlife Service quoted the Gordens expressing satisfaction with the restoration, the wildlife using their property and the support they received from their conservation partners. articles.title: Reform activist suspended after reportedly saying Muslims cannot be British
articles.summary: The alleged comments were filmed by an undercover reporter for an ITV broadcast: Undercover a Year in Reform
articles.body:
Reform UK has suspended a party activist who reportedly said that you cannot be Muslim and British in footage recorded by an undercover reporter from ITV News.

It is also investigating two of its councillors who appear to have advocated for the mass shooting of grooming gang members in the footage.

The party's response follows the latest allegations from undercover filming by ITV News , which has led to Reform facing questions over its vetting procedures for candidates.

A party spokesperson told the BBC it was pursuing legal action against ITV and the documentary's production company which had used undercover reporting to obtain its material.

In the ITV documentary Undercover: A Year in Reform - set to be broadcast on Sunday - party activist Jason Powell reportedly says: "You cannot be Muslim and British, it's like oil and water."

In the footage, Powell, who has applied to be a Reform parliamentary candidate, also says he believes migrants who arrive illegally should be kept in "concentration camps" if they cannot be returned to their country of origin.

Reform said Powell has been suspended from party membership while an internal investigation takes place.

Reform is also investigating two councillors who represent the party in the London borough of Hounslow.

In the footage, Councillor David Kerr advocates machine gunning thousands of grooming gang members.

His colleague Councillor Adam Parkins suggests if he became prime minister he would conduct Sunday morning executions in the Downing Street rose garden.

Mr Parkins told the BBC that advocating the death penalty for men who "systemically groomed and raped young girls" was a perfectly legitimate opinion.

In a statement to ITV, Reform said there is "no room for racism" in the party, and added that it has opened investigations where activists or members had "clearly behaved inappropriately".

Reform UK has said it has prioritised and improved its vetting procedures.

On Wednesday night, ITV News broadcast undercover filming which showed some of Reform's councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language .

Responding to the broadcast, Reform UK MP Robert Jenrick said all political parties had "bad apples".

Speaking to the BBC's Today programme, he said he "didn't like what I heard in the documentary" but argued that the party had acted quickly, removing or suspending those in the undercover film.

articles.title: Cost of living protests hit Belgium, Italy, Portugal and France
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands took to the streets for separate demonstrations putting pressure on governments across the EU.
articles.body:
Hundreds of thousands of Europeans have taken to the streets in separate, uncoordinated demonstrations to protest against the rising cost of living in their countries.

Saturday’s protests were in Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal in a wave of unrest that has put pressure on national governments across the European Union.

France experienced one of its most turbulent days of protests in decades, with over 550,000 people joining demonstrations and police facing off with protesters across the country – but it was not the only country to see significant demonstrations.

In Belgium’s capital Brussels – which has already seen weeks of protests by students against university registration fees – police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters, who they accused of launching missiles at them and setting fires.

In Liege, a smaller city east of Brussels, police also deployed water cannon to break up demonstrations. Police did not say how many people attended.

An estimated tens of thousands of protesters marched in Lisbon, the Portuguese capital, against the cost of living crisis, low wages and an inability to access housing in major cities. House prices in Portugal have more than doubled ⁠⁠since 2017, while rents for new leases have increased nearly as much.

Portuguese Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos ‌‌Abreu ‌‌Amorim said on Friday that the “government will not yield to shouts from the street”.Protesters said their leaders are “out of touch” with the problem.

In Milan and Bologna, Italian police reported that, alongside peaceful cost of living rallies, protesters threw stones and clashed with officers.

Italian media reported several injuries and arrests.

None of the protests reached the same scale as the nationwide rallies in France but they may be a sign of spilling over into other European nations, according to Alberto Alemanno, Professor of EU Law & Policy at HEC Paris business school.

“France is the epicentre of this movement … and there are signs now that this is spreading beyond France,” Alemanno told Al Jazeera.

He said Saturday’s protests may not be the last in many of these countries and new hotspots could emerge.

In Greece, Germany, and Austria, the “early stages” of a movement is emerging, with mobilisation expected “in the coming week”, he said.

They are not a single movement, he explained, but several protests happening at the same time, with some “shared grievances”: underfunded education, rising costs and, for students, uncertain prospects after graduation.

The unrest comes at a crucial time for Europe, as the continent prepares for what Alemanno called an “unprecedented super-cycle of national elections” in the coming 12 months, with votes scheduled in Spain, France, Italy and Poland.

“Inevitably, all these protests, all these mobilisations, are going to be at the centre of the political conversation,” Alemanno said.

articles.title: Photos: No Kings rallies in US urge midterm voters to cast ballots early
articles.summary: Thousands gathered at events throughout the country on Saturday, building on two years of No Kings marches.
articles.body:
Rallies organised by the No Kings network opposed to United States President Donald Trump were held Saturday in cities and communities across the US, with an aim of getting people out to vote early in the midterm elections.

No Kings has more than 3,000 events planned across the US. The planned events, this time dubbed “No Kings: Vote Early”, were billed as nonpartisan, though they sought to build on nearly two years’ worth of No Kings marches and demonstrations by people upset with Trump’s presidency.

“It’s a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard,” organisers said in a statement.

By advocating for voting early, the “No Kings” organisers hope to cut off the potential for any malfeasance once election day rolls around.

A band entertained what appeared to be a few hundred people in caps and coats at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, DC. Despite the chilly weather, many in the crowd danced to the tunes. “VOTE EARLY” and “HANDS OFF MY VOTE!” were among the many signs held aloft.

At an Atlanta rally, City Councilman Michael Julian Bond told the crowd to urge others to vote ahead of the November 3 general election.

“The Constitution gives you one power, right? That is the power to vote. Are you gonna use that power?” he said.

“You don’t see Superman giving up his power,” Bond continued. “You don’t see Black Panther giving up his power. You don’t see Wonder Woman giving up her magic lasso. So why would you give up your right, your power, your obligation to vote? Be a superhero, use your power. Go to the polls and vote.”

Trump has long been suspicious of mail voting and has claimed without evidence that voting fraud cost him the 2020 presidential election.

His administration sued California election officials Thursday , asking a judge to bar the state from counting mail-in ballots for the midterm elections from people whom the federal government has identified as “likely” noncitizens until their immigration status can be confirmed.

On Friday, the Department of Justice warned that local officials who process and tabulate ballots submitted by suspected noncitizen voters are putting themselves at risk of criminal investigation and potential prosecution.

Earlier that day, Democratic Senators Alex Padilla of California, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island and Dick Durbin of Illinois wrote to Attorney General Todd Blanche, demanding that the Justice Department commit to not seizing ballots or other election materials before the midterm elections are certified.

articles.title: A cow escaped a California slaughterhouse truck; Diane Warren helped give the animal a new life at a sanctuary
articles.summary: A cow that escaped from a slaughterhouse in Pico Rivera, California, in June 2021 was given a chance at a different life after Grammy-winning songwriter
articles.body: A cow that escaped from a slaughterhouse in Pico Rivera, California, in June 2021 was given a chance at a different life after Grammy-winning songwriter Diane Warren stepped in to help. The animal was one of around 40 cows that broke free from a meatpacking facility and ran through nearby streets. While most of the herd was quickly recovered, one cow remained missing for more than a day. Her eventual capture attracted attention, but it was Warren’s intervention that helped turn the incident into a story of rescue and renewed hope.How the rescuers captured the escaped California cowAccording to the AP, the incident began on the evening of 22 June 2021, when around 40 cows escaped from a slaughterhouse in Pico Rivera, a suburb of Los Angeles. The animals ran into the surrounding neighbourhood, creating an unexpected scene for residents and prompting efforts to bring them under control.The escape drew attention as the cows moved through public areas rather than remaining inside the facility. Most were recovered, but one animal continued to evade capture. Her disappearance extended the search and eventually led rescuers to a nearby recreation area.PETA also reported on the escape, sharing video footage of the cows running loose and highlighting the dangers they faced.The cow was spotted before dawn on Thursday at the Whittier Narrows recreation area in South El Monte, several miles from the slaughterhouse. Two wranglers attempted to restrain her using lassoes, while Los Angeles County sheriff’s deputies helped keep her away from nearby traffic.The capture proved difficult. The cow knocked down and kicked one of the wranglers during the operation. Despite the struggle, the rescuers eventually managed to bring her under control.The search had ended, but the cow’s future was still uncertain. Being captured meant she could no longer run through the surrounding area, yet it did not automatically mean she would avoid being returned to the slaughterhouse.The cow needed somewhere safe to go, and Warren became involved in efforts to arrange precisely that.Diane Warren helped arrange a sanctuary placementWarren, an award-winning songwriter known for her work in the music industry, was moved by the reports of the escape. According to the AP, she contacted officials in Pico Rivera to help arrange for the missing cow to be sent to Farm Sanctuary, an organisation that provides a home for rescued farm animals.Pico Rivera City Manager Steve Carmona confirmed that Warren had approached the city about the animal’s future. Her involvement helped bring attention to the possibility of giving the cow a life away from the meat industry.Local animal activist Simone Reyes was also involved in the rescue effort, according to information from Farm Sanctuary cited in PETA’s report. The involvement of animal advocates and local officials helped move the arrangements forward.Farm Sanctuary offered the cow a different futureFarm Sanctuary was identified as the intended destination for the rescued cow. The organisation provides care for farm animals rescued from situations in which they face harm, giving them a place to live outside the usual agricultural system. AP reported that the transfer depended on a health check by state agriculture officials. This step was necessary before the cow could move to her new home.The escape drew attention to farm animal welfareThe incident prompted wider discussion about the treatment of farm animals. For people who watched footage of the cows running through California streets, the escape offered a glimpse of animals suddenly outside the controlled environment in which they were being kept.PETA used its coverage to encourage people to think about the lives of animals raised for food.Warren’s involvement was central to securing the proposed sanctuary placement. By contacting city officials, she helped turn concern over the escape into an effort to find the cow a safer home. The rescue did not change the outcome for the entire herd, but it gave the missing cow a chance to live beyond the fate originally intended for her.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Ex-wrestler Pac's sudden death cause revealed by Cook County Medical Examiner's Office
articles.summary: Benjamin Satterley, known as Pac, died of bronchial asthma at 40, just one day after competing for the AEW National Championship at All Out.
articles.body: Former wrestling star Pac, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, died of bronchial asthma late last month, the California Post said, citing the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office. Pac was 40 years old when All Elite Wrestling (AEW) announced his death. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac," the company said. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans." He challenged Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out, which occurred just one day before his death. Pac was found dead in a rental car the next day outside of a CAVA outside of Chicago, where that bout occurred. Officers saw his phone's GPS guiding him to O'Hare airport. PRO WRESTLER TAKING HIS SHOT AT RUNNING HIS OWN INDEPENDENT SHOW: 'LET'S JUST TAKE IT UP A NOTCH' Pac was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion. Before wrestling in AEW, he was with WWE and known as Adrian Neville. articles.title: Prices of 137 cancer drugs to fall by up to 70% from November 9
articles.summary: In good news for cancer patients, prices of 137 drugs are set to be reduced by up to 70% from Nov 9, with govt capping trade margins by 30%.
articles.body: In good news for cancer patients, prices of 137 drugs are set to be reduced by up to 70% from Nov 9, with govt capping trade margins by 30%. Drug prices regulator National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) Saturday notified the 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs to address the issue of excessive trade margins, invoking Paragraph 19 of DPCO, 2013. Significantly, patented drugs are also included in the list.The trade margin rationalisation at 30% of MRP, excluding GST, corresponds to a mark-up of 42.9% on price to stockist/price to distributor (PTS/PTD), according to the minutes of the NPPA meeting accessed by TOI. Simply put, PTS/PTD is the first point of sale of the drug.This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients, in certain cases of 10 times.The MRPs of certain drugs — including pertuzumab + trastuzumab, atezolizumab, teclistamab, inotuzumab ozogamicin and daratumumab — are up to Rs 5 lakh per vial/pack.All manufacturers will be required to inform NPPA of their revised prices within seven days of publication of the gazette notification. Manufacturers will be req-uired to display the price lists on their website and widely disseminate them to all retailers and hospitals, with the latter also required to display the revised prices on their websites prominently.The authority approved the calculation of the revised MRP based on PTS/PTD for March 2026 as the reference month.NPPA said patient assistance programme quantities may be excluded from the calculation of PTS/PTD and MRP for trade-margin capping only. These programmes, where drugs are supplied free of cost, are typically run by MNCs.As a substantial supply of anti-cancer drugs is directly made to hospitals and medical institutions, they shall be responsible for ensuring revised prices of such drugs from the date of implementation, NPPA said. State drug controllers will take necessary steps to ensure compliance by manufacturers, dealers including retailers, hospitals and medical institutions, it added.In a bid to tighten rules further, NPPA said uninterrupted availability of the covered formulations needed to be ensured. Any manufacturer intending to reduce monthly production levels would have to obtain permission.Consumers can use the Pharma Sahi Daam app and NPPA website to check revised prices of drugs, an official release said.In 2019, the MRP of 526 brands of non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines was reduced by up to 90%, NPPA said. The present exercise extends this approach to a larger set of drugs, based on the list recommended by an expert committee under Directorate General of Health Services.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
